name: LoginBrigade – Page Designer, Magic Links, Passkeys & 2FA
author: brigadethemes

sections.description:
LoginBrigade gives your WordPress login page your brand, adds easier ways to log in, and keeps attackers out. The look is designed live in the WordPress Customizer; everything else is set up from one dashboard where every screen, save and action works instantly without reloading the page. Every feature is free.

Live login page designer (WordPress Customizer)

  • Appearance → Customize → LoginBrigade shows your real login page in the preview and updates it as you work. Nothing goes live until you press Publish (drafts and scheduling work too).
  • 31 templates with real thumbnails – 5 essentials (Modern, Classic, Minimal, Dark, Corporate), 14 Blue glass designs (Aurora Glass, Frost, Clean Slate, Harbor Split, Midnight, Paper, Nebula, Studio Split, Graphite, Shapes, Skyline, Ocean Glass, Minimal Ink, Split Photo) and 12 cinematic designs: Cinematic Dark, Luxury Glassmorphism, Neon Cyberpunk, Futuristic AI, Minimalist Premium, Dark Gradient, Elegant Gold, Modern Aurora, Space & Galaxy, Animated Abstract, Frosted Glass and High-End Corporate. Click one to try it; it brings its own fonts, colours, shapes and animated background.
  • 13 setting groups with icons: Templates, General, Layout & Position, Typography & Fonts, Colors & Backgrounds, Buttons & Icons, Input Fields, Borders & Shadows, Animations & Transitions, Hover Effects, Fingerprint Button, Responsive Settings, and Text & Messages. Sub-groups fold away, every slider has a reset, and a Preview bar switches between log in, register, lost password, magic link and email code.
  • Fonts: the included Urbanist font, system or serif fonts, with sizes and weights. Optional Google Fonts (off until you turn them on): searchable picker with a live preview, separate fonts for text, headings, buttons and fields; 58 hand-picked fonts, or all of them with a free Google Fonts API key. Only the fonts and weights in use are loaded, only on login screens.
  • Normal, hover, focus and pressed states: button background, text and border on hover, grow and lift, press size, field hover and focus colour and ring, link and icon hover colours, transition speed and easing.
  • Glass and backgrounds: gradients, background image with size, position and darkening, form opacity and background blur.
  • Background video and slideshow: play a muted, looping video (from the Media Library, a YouTube or Vimeo link, or any .mp4/.webm address) or cycle through a gallery of images with fade, zoom or slide transitions. On split templates they fill the brand panel. Visitors who ask for less motion see a still image.
  • Messages & alerts: style error (wrong password, attempts left), success and information messages – card with coloured bar, soft tint, solid, outline or minimal, with your own colours, icons, text size, corners, shadow and alignment. Sample messages show in the Customizer preview while you edit.
  • Brand panel options for split templates: its own colour, text colour, image and darkening.
  • Motion: form entrance (fade, slide, zoom, tilt), animated backgrounds that can be switched off – and none at all for visitors who ask their device for less motion.
  • Fingerprint button: under the Log In button, at the top or bottom of the form, or below it; full width, left, centre or right – separately for desktop, tablet and phone; size, style, spacing and fine offsets.
  • Responsive settings for form width, padding, logo and text size per device, synced with the Customizer’s device buttons.
  • Heading and subheading above the form, messages and footer text.

Fingerprint and face login (passkeys)

  • “Log in with fingerprint or face” on the login page: Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello, Android fingerprint or screen lock, and passkeys saved in Google Password Manager, iCloud Keychain or 1Password.
  • No username or password to type. Users add a passkey once on their profile page (up to 10 devices) and can remove any of them.
  • The fingerprint or face never leaves the device; the site stores only a public key. Passkeys only work on your site’s address, so they can’t be phished.
  • Counts as two factors, so the separate two-factor step is skipped. Can be kept away from administrators.
  • The button only appears on laptops and phones that have a fingerprint or face scanner; everyone else simply sees the username and password form.
  • After a password login on a device with a scanner, the dashboard offers to set up fingerprint login (“Not now” hides it).
  • New users can skip the password entirely: the “set your password” page that the registration email links to offers “Use fingerprint or face instead”. One touch adds the passkey and uses up the link; they then log in with it on the login form. (It comes after the email step on purpose – that link proves the address is theirs. It only works in the browser that opened the link, and accounts with two-step login set a password instead and add a passkey from their profile.)
  • Sessions show how each one signed in (password, fingerprint, magic link, …).
  • Needs HTTPS (as all browsers require).

Passwordless login

  • Magic link: “Email me a login link instead”. Links are 256-bit random, single use, expire (5–60 minutes) and stored only as a hash. The link opens a “Log in” button so email scanners can’t use it up.
  • Email code: a 6-digit code by email, with an expiry, a limited number of tries and a resend wait.
  • Both give the same answer whether or not an account exists, are rate limited per address and per account, can be limited to roles or kept away from administrators, and have editable email templates.

Google and Microsoft login

  • “Continue with Google” and “Continue with Microsoft” (personal, work or school accounts, or only your organisation).
  • OpenID Connect with state, nonce and PKCE; the ID token signature, issuer, audience and expiry are checked.
  • Safe account linking: an existing account is linked only when Google confirms the email address – or only from the user’s profile, your choice. Users can connect and disconnect accounts on their profile page.
  • Optionally create accounts for new Google users (when “Anyone can register” is on). Administrators can be kept on passwords.

Two-factor authentication

  • Authenticator app codes (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…) set up from the profile page with a QR code.
  • 10 single-use recovery codes; new codes need the current password.
  • Required for chosen roles (set up at the next login), optional for everyone else.
  • “Remember this device” for 1–30 days (forgotten when the password changes).
  • Applies to every login method: password, magic link, email code, Google and Microsoft.
  • Administrators can reset a user’s two-factor; the reset is recorded.

Login security

  • Lockouts: lock out an address after too many failed logins in a time window. IPv6 networks are grouped by /64.
  • Account protection: when one account is attacked from many addresses, only addresses it used before can log in with its password.
  • Hide login hints on the login and lost-password forms.
  • IP rules: allow and block lists for addresses and ranges (IPv4 and IPv6), with notes and expiry. Blocking your own address needs confirmation.
  • Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA on log in, register, lost password, magic link and email code forms, with a choice of what happens if Cloudflare can’t be reached.
  • Custom login address (example.com/my-login): wp-login.php and logged-out /wp-admin/ show “not found”; an emergency switch for wp-config.php.
  • Trusted proxies (Cloudflare, load balancers) so lockouts use the real visitor address.
  • Disable XML-RPC (off by default) and block username discovery (?author= links and the REST API users list for logged-out visitors).
  • Login Activity: see who is signed in now, how and from which device; end a single session, block an account (it can’t log in by any method until unblocked, and its content stays) or block an address in one click.
  • Analytics: sign-ins per day by method, passwordless share, why logins failed, devices and a weekday/hour heatmap – all from the plugin’s own log, nothing sent anywhere.
  • Sessions: users see where they’re logged in and can end any session; administrators can log users out everywhere.
  • Security events: logins, failures, lockouts, codes, social logins, two-factor and setting changes, with filters and CSV export. IP addresses stored as a fingerprint by default; kept 30 days by default.
  • Alerts: email users about logins from new addresses, email yourself about lockouts, optional Slack webhook.

Redirects and login forms

  • Send administrators, other users or each role to different pages after logging in, and choose where logout goes. Redirects to the login page are refused so nobody gets stuck in a loop.
  • Login form on any page with the “LoginBrigade Login Form” block or the [loginbrigade_login] shortcode.

Built to the BrigadeThemes standard

  • Fully AJAX dashboard: screens, saves and actions never reload the page (and still work without JavaScript).
  • Setup checklist, test email and test magic link, settings export/import (secrets are never exported), reset, diagnostics.
  • No tracking and no external requests unless you turn on Google, Microsoft, Turnstile or Slack. Client secrets, keys and webhooks are stored encrypted.
  • Works with the WordPress personal data export and erase tools.
  • Translation ready.

Hooks

  • loginbrigade_client_ip (filter): the visitor IP used for lockouts and rules.
  • loginbrigade_magic_link_allowed (filter): allow or block magic links per user.
  • loginbrigade_magic_email (filter): change the magic link email (to, subject, message, headers).
  • loginbrigade_magic_requests_limit (filter): link requests per IP per 15 minutes.
  • loginbrigade_lockout (action): runs when an address is locked out.
  • loginbrigade_otp_allowed, loginbrigade_otp_email (filters): email codes per user, and the code email.
  • loginbrigade_authentication_methods, loginbrigade_authentication_method_allowed (filters): list or refuse login methods per user.
  • loginbrigade_two_factor_required (filter): require two-factor for a user.
  • loginbrigade_passkey_allowed, loginbrigade_passkey_rp_id, loginbrigade_passkey_origins (filters): passkeys per user, and the site name/addresses passkeys are tied to.
  • loginbrigade_ip_blocked, loginbrigade_turnstile_result (filters).
  • loginbrigade_after_login, loginbrigade_security_event, loginbrigade_settings_saved, loginbrigade_two_factor_reset (actions).
  • loginbrigade_new_login_email (filter): the “new login” email.

Privacy

LoginBrigade records security events (event type, time, user, result and the IP address – as a one-way fingerprint by default, in full or not at all if you choose). Events are deleted after 30 days by default and are included in WordPress’s personal data export and erase tools. Login links, codes, recovery codes, tokens and passwords are never logged. For passkeys only a public key and the device name you choose are stored; fingerprints and faces never reach the site. Google Fonts are off by default; they are loaded from Google only after you turn on “Use Google Fonts” in the Customizer and pick one (the visitor’s browser requests them; bundled Urbanist and system fonts make no request). Nothing else is sent to other services unless you use a YouTube or Vimeo background video (the visitor’s browser loads that player) or turn on Google or Microsoft login (sign-in with those providers), Cloudflare Turnstile (the CAPTCHA answer and visitor IP are checked with Cloudflare) or Slack alerts.

External services

LoginBrigade works fully on its own. It connects to the services below only when you turn the matching feature on. Nothing is sent to BrigadeThemes.

Google Fonts (Google) – loads the fonts you pick in the login page designer.

  • When: only after you turn on “Use Google Fonts” (Customizer → Typography & Fonts, off by default) and select a Google font. Templates never turn it on. The bundled Urbanist font and system fonts make no request.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser requests the font files from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com when it opens the login page, which shares the visitor’s IP address and browser details with Google. If you add a Google Fonts API key, your site also requests the font list from www.googleapis.com (sending the key) while you browse fonts in the Customizer.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy · Google Fonts privacy FAQ

Google sign-in (Google OpenID Connect) – “Continue with Google”.

  • When: only when Google login is turned on and a visitor clicks the button.
  • What is sent: the visitor is sent to accounts.google.com to sign in. Your site then sends the sign-in code, your client ID and client secret to oauth2.googleapis.com and downloads Google’s public keys from www.googleapis.com to check the result. Google returns the user’s account ID, name and email address.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy

Microsoft sign-in (Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft account) – “Continue with Microsoft”.

  • When: only when Microsoft login is turned on and a visitor clicks the button.
  • What is sent: the visitor is sent to login.microsoftonline.com to sign in. Your site then sends the sign-in code, your client ID and client secret to login.microsoftonline.com and downloads Microsoft’s public keys from the same address to check the result. Microsoft returns the user’s account ID, name and email address.
  • Terms of use · Privacy statement

Cloudflare Turnstile (Cloudflare) – CAPTCHA on the login, registration and lost password forms.

  • When: only when Turnstile is turned on with your site and secret keys.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser loads the Turnstile script from challenges.cloudflare.com, which checks the browser. When a form is sent, your site sends the Turnstile answer, your secret key and the visitor’s IP address to challenges.cloudflare.com to verify it.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy · Turnstile privacy addendum

YouTube (Google) – background video on the login page.

  • When: only when you choose “Video” as the background type and paste a YouTube link. Visitors who ask for less motion do not load it.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser loads the player from www.youtube-nocookie.com (YouTube’s privacy-enhanced mode) when it opens the login page, which shares the visitor’s IP address and browser details with Google.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy

Vimeo (Vimeo.com, Inc.) – background video on the login page.

  • When: only when you choose “Video” as the background type and paste a Vimeo link. Visitors who ask for less motion do not load it.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser loads the player from player.vimeo.com (with “do not track” on) when it opens the login page, which shares the visitor’s IP address and browser details with Vimeo.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy

Slack (Slack Technologies) – security alerts in a Slack channel.

  • When: only when you add a Slack webhook URL in Settings.
  • What is sent: a short alert message (event type, username and your site’s address) to the hooks.slack.com webhook you entered.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin in Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin and activate it.
  2. Open LoginBrigade in the admin menu and follow the setup checklist on the Overview screen.
  3. Click Open live designer (or go to Appearance → Customize → LoginBrigade) to design the login page.
sections.faq:
Will I get locked out of my own site?

Only after the number of failed attempts you set, and only for the lockout time you set. If it happens, add define( 'LOGINBRIGADE_NO_LOCKOUT', true ); to wp-config.php, log in, unlock your address on Security → Lockouts and remove the line. Add your own address as an “Allow” IP rule and it’s never locked out.

I changed the login address and forgot it

The new address was emailed to the site admin email. Or add define( 'LOGINBRIGADE_DISABLE_LOGIN_URL', true ); to wp-config.php to bring back wp-login.php.

My site is behind Cloudflare or a proxy

Add the proxy’s address ranges under Security → Lockouts → Trusted proxies and pick the header it sends (CF-Connecting-IP for Cloudflare). Headers from anyone else are ignored because they can be faked. The dashboard warns you when it detects an unconfigured proxy.

Someone lost their phone

They can log in with a recovery code. If they lost those too, open their user profile and click “Reset two-factor for this user”.

Does it work with user approval or email verification plugins?

Yes. Every LoginBrigade login method runs the same wp_authenticate_user check as a password login, so those plugins can still refuse a login.

Why the Customizer instead of a settings page?

The Customizer shows the real login page and updates it while you work, with drafts, scheduling and Publish built in – the same way you design the rest of your site. All settings are shared with the dashboard.

Does LoginBrigade read my fingerprint?

No. Your phone or computer checks your fingerprint or face itself and then signs a one-time challenge. The site only receives that signature and keeps a public key – nothing about your fingerprint or face.

Passkeys don’t show on the login page

They need HTTPS and a browser that supports them (current Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox do). Users also need to add a passkey on their profile page first.

Why is Apple sign-in not included?

It’s planned. It needs an Apple developer account to test properly, and we don’t ship login code we couldn’t test end to end.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Live login page designer in the WordPress Customizer: 31 templates (5 essentials, 12 cinematic and 14 Blue glass designs), Google Fonts picker, colours, layout, hover/focus/pressed states, glass effects, motion, and responsive settings.
  • Passkeys: log in with a fingerprint, face or screen lock (WebAuthn), including a passkey instead of a password for new accounts.
  • Passwordless login with magic links and email codes.
  • Google and Microsoft login with safe account linking.
  • Two-factor authentication with authenticator apps and recovery codes, required per role.
  • Login security: lockouts, IP allow/block rules, Cloudflare Turnstile, custom login address, account protection, trusted proxies, IPv6 /64 grouping, disable XML-RPC and block username discovery.
  • Dashboard with analytics, login activity (end sessions, block accounts or addresses) and integrations overview.
  • Security events with filters, CSV export, retention and privacy tools; alerts by email and Slack.
  • Session management, per-role redirects, login form block and shortcode, email templates.
  • Setup checklist, test email, settings export/import, reset and diagnostics.

Microsoft sign-in (Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft account) – “Continue with Microsoft”.

  • When: only when Microsoft login is turned on and a visitor clicks the button.
  • What is sent: the visitor is sent to login.microsoftonline.com to sign in. Your site then sends the sign-in code, your client ID and client secret to login.microsoftonline.com and downloads Microsoft’s public keys from the same address to check the result. Microsoft returns the user’s account ID, name and email address.
  • Terms of use · Privacy statement

Cloudflare Turnstile (Cloudflare) – CAPTCHA on the login, registration and lost password forms.

  • When: only when Turnstile is turned on with your site and secret keys.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser loads the Turnstile script from challenges.cloudflare.com, which checks the browser. When a form is sent, your site sends the Turnstile answer, your secret key and the visitor’s IP address to challenges.cloudflare.com to verify it.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy · Turnstile privacy addendum

YouTube (Google) – background video on the login page.

  • When: only when you choose “Video” as the background type and paste a YouTube link. Visitors who ask for less motion do not load it.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser loads the player from www.youtube-nocookie.com (YouTube’s privacy-enhanced mode) when it opens the login page, which shares the visitor’s IP address and browser details with Google.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy

Vimeo (Vimeo.com, Inc.) – background video on the login page.

  • When: only when you choose “Video” as the background type and paste a Vimeo link. Visitors who ask for less motion do not load it.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser loads the player from player.vimeo.com (with “do not track” on) when it opens the login page, which shares the visitor’s IP address and browser details with Vimeo.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy

Slack (Slack Technologies) – security alerts in a Slack channel.

  • When: only when you add a Slack webhook URL in Settings.
  • What is sent: a short alert message (event type, username and your site’s address) to the hooks.slack.com webhook you entered.
  • Terms of service · Privacy policy
